en: Jose Rizal was executed by a Spanish firing squad at Bagumbayan on December 30, 1896.
The Philippine eagle, known for its shaggy crest, is the national bird of the Philippines.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines is the highest tribunal and leads the judicial branch of government.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-step forward dance.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato are renowned for weaving intricate T'nalak cloth from abaca fibers.
Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to help provide healthcare for infants in rural areas.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses specific characters to represent syllables.
Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition for his painting Spoliarium.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Filipino citizens must be at least eighteen years old to register and vote in national elections.
